summary: Local schools have expanded extracurricular programs since the academic term began on September 1, 2023, aiming to boost student engagement and holistic development. The note surveys initiatives in sports, arts, technology, language/culture, debate, and community-building clubs at several named schools. It cites Dr. Helen Fischer's research linking extracurriculars to better social skills, self-esteem, and academic achievement.
one_line: Local schools expanded extracurricular programs in fall 2023 across sports, arts, tech, language and debate to foster engaged, well-rounded students.
key_facts: The academic term began on September 1, 2023, and local education systems have since expanded extracurricular offerings.
Charles Madison, principal of Elmwood High School, announced an initiative on September 12 'to foster a more engaged, well-rounded student body.'
Rosemary Academy and Northside Middle School mirrored Elmwood High School's extracurricular expansion.

Dr. Helen Fischer, a developmental psychologist, presented findings on October 5, 2023, that extracurricular students show improved social skills, higher self-esteem, and elevated academic achievement.
Vice Principal Angela Thompson led 'The Mosaic Project' at Harmony Intermediate School, launched September 22, 2023, combining various clubs under one umbrella.
Coach Larry Johnson unveiled the 'Leadership through Sports' program at Westbrook High on September 15, focusing on sportsmanship, perseverance, and dedication.
Sofia Rodriguez of Sunnyside Elementary introduced an art program on October 1, 2023, saying 'Art is a universal language that every child can speak.'
Thomas Bradley, a computer science teacher at Innovation Tech High, started the 'Code for Future' club on September 20.
Maria Gonzalez, a Spanish teacher, founded 'The Global Village' club at Crescentwood Middle School on October 10 and has seen growing student interest.
Frederick Daniels leads the debate team at Oakleaf High School, which began on September 18 and discusses current issues to sharpen critical thinking and public speaking.
Activities range from sports teams and technology clubs to art workshops and debate teams, chosen to reach every student demographic.
Tech clubs are described as preparing students for STEM careers and promoting digital literacy.
